Answer

1  She often borrows my clothes, but she never owns up to it.

2   I asked for a seat by the window.

3   The police officer looked at my passport carefully.

4   Are you talking about the World cup?

5   I found out where my brother hides his diary.

Writing Strategy

When you write a description of an event, remember to say how you and other people felt at the time, and how you all reacted to the events. This will make your anecdote come to life and engage the readerâ€™s interest.

2. Read the Writing Strategy. Then complete the description using the adjectives below describe the peopleâ€™s feelings.

guilty      proud      scared      upset

Confession!

Joanne

I once bought a big plastic insect at a joke shop and put it inside my brotherâ€™s lunch box in the morning. It looked disgusting! I told my friends about the prank â€“ I was1â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ of it! My brother didnâ€™t say anything about it after school. In fact, he didnâ€™t mention it for ages. Then one morning I found the same insect in my bowl of cereal at breakfast. I wasnâ€™t2â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ at all â€“ it was funny. But when I asked him how he felt when he found it in his lunch box, he didnâ€™t smile. In fact he hooked a bit3â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ â€˜It was horrible,â€™ he said. â€˜I screamed. Then everybody laughed at me.â€™ When I heard that, I felt really4â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ I donâ€™t play tricks on my brother now!

Answer

Writing Guide

3. Read the task. Then make brief notes in the table below. Use one of the suggestions in the ideas box or your own idea.

You did something you feel bad about. Write a description of an event with the little â€˜Confession!â€™

â€“  Give a short description of what you did.

â€“  Say how you felt at the time.

â€“  Describe how other people reacted.

â€“  Explain why you feel bad about it now.

Notes

What did you do?

  

How did you feel at the time? Why?

  

How did other people feel? How did they react?

  

How do you feel about it now? Why?

  

Ideas

You feel bad because you:

â€“  borrowed something without asking and broke it.

â€“  told somebody a secret your friend told you.

â€“  copied some homework from the internet.

â€“  told somebody about a surprise party and spoiled the surprise.

Answer

4. Write your description. Use your notes from exercise 3.

Extra exercises

Strategy

Read the question carefully and make sure you understand what types of text you need to write. Think carefully about how formal or informal your writing needs to be.

1. Read the Strategy. Then read the exam task and a studentâ€™s answer. Underline words and phrases that show you that the email was written to a friend.

You have recently been on holiday with your family. Write an email about it to a friend in Britain. Include the following points:

â€“  where you went

â€“  how you got there

â€“  something interesting you did

â€“  how you felt when you got home

â€“  an invitation to your friend to stay with you for the next school holiday.

Hi David,

How are things? Iâ€™m depressed! I went on holiday to the south of France with my family last week and I didnâ€™t want to come home! We had a brilliant time.

We travelled by plane to Marseille and then by coach to a seaside town. We stayed in a lovely hotel. It was right on the beach.

One day we went to a small restaurant and we had an amazing meal. We had loads of seafood â€“ delicious! The restaurant was on a hill with a lovely view of the sea. It was really cool.

When we got home yesterday I started to get anxious about my school exams next week. I need to think about another holiday! So, why donâ€™t you come and stay with us in the summer? We can have a great time!

Write soon,

Katy

Answer

your own answers

â€“  type of event and its location

â€“  the atmosphere at the event

â€“  what you enjoyed most

3. Read the Writing Strategy opposite. Then write the missing words to complete the letter below.

I enjoyed the film, but I didnâ€™t think it was brilliant. There are some exciting scenes, but itâ€™s really long and I got a bit bored by the end.

Before the film, we made pizzas and popcorn. We ate them while we were watching the film. (The pizza was a bit burned!)

Writing Strategy

When you write a letter to a friend or relative:

â€“  Start with:Dear[Jake],.

â€“  Begin the main part of the letter with a short introduction. You can use phrases like:How are you? Sorry I didnâ€™t reply sooner. Thanks for your letter.

â€“  Write in paragraphs.

â€“  Do not use very formal language in your letter.

â€“  Use contractions (itâ€™s, thereâ€™s,etc.).

â€“  Finish the main part of the letter with a short paragraph. You can use phrases like:Thatâ€™s all for now. Iâ€™d better go now. Write again soon.

â€“  End the letter withLove,orBest wishes, and your first name.

5. Read the task below. Underline the parts of Paigeâ€™s letter which give extra information about each of the four points.

English Writing Exercises for A2 â€“ An article

Preparation

1. Complete the zero conditional sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets.

1  If you â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (burn) coal, it â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (give) off greenhouse gases.

2  A rainbow often â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (appear) if the sun â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (come) out when itâ€™s raining.

3  If an earthquake â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (happen) under the ocean, it sometimes â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (cause) a tsunami.

4  If a hurricane â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (form) over the Indian Ocean, they â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (call) it a typhoon.

5  If you â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (eat) ice, it â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (make) your body cold.

6  Floods â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (happen) if it â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ (rain) a lot more than usual for a long time.

Answer

1burn, gives  2 appears, comes  3 happens, causes

4forms, call  5 eat, makes  6 happen, rains

Writing Strategy

When you are expressing your opinions and the opinions of others, give your text a clear structure. For example:

â€“  In one paragraph, give your opinion with two or three arguments that support it.

â€“  In another paragraphs, give the opposing view with one or two arguments supporting it. You can then say why you disagree with the opposing view (a counter-argument)

2. Read the Writing Strategy. Then read the task below and the model text. Decide where the second paragraph should begin: A, B or C.

English Writing Exercises for A2 â€“ An opinion essay

Preparation

1. Read the task and the essay. Are the sentences true (T) or false (F)?

1  Sarah wants a sound system because she hasnâ€™t got anything for listening to music.

2  Her brother loves football.

3  Sheâ€™d give money to an organisation that helps homeless people.

4  Sheâ€™d spend most of the money.

If you won â‚¬1 million in the lottery, what would you do with it? Write an essay and include your ideas. Give reasons for your choices.

If I won â‚¬1 million, there are a lot of things I would like to do with the money. It would be nice to buy myself something, but it would also be good to help others.

First of all, I would buy myself a docking station with fantastic speakers. Although I have got an MP3 player and some speakers, they are not very good.

Secondly, I would buy a new car for my mum. Her car is really old. I would buy my brother a Liverpool kit and a scarf. He is a really big Liverpool fan!

Thirdly, there are a lot of homeless people in my city. I would donate money to the local hostel. If I gave them â‚¬5,000, they could buy a lot of meals for homeless people.

Finally, I would save at least half of the money. In my opinion, it would be silly to spend it all now. What is more, if I invested the money, it would grow, and I would have more to spend in the future.

To sum up, I would buy something nice for myself and other members of my family, support local charities, and also save some money for the future.

Answer

1 F  2 T  3 T  4 F

Writing Strategy

In your writing, avoid starting too many sentences with the same words. Remember that you can:

â€“  use a variety of phrases for introducing opinions (It seems to me â€¦, In my opinion â€¦,etc.) and for making additional points (Moreover â€¦, Furthermore â€¦,etc.)

â€“  start conditional sentences with theifclause or the main clause.

â€“  use concession clauses (although â€¦/even though â€¦) at the beginning or end of a sentence.

Strategy

When writing an essay you need to make sure you structure your work carefully and divide it into paragraphs. Guide the reader through your points by starting your paragraphs with words such as,First of all, Secondly,andFinally.

1. Read the Strategy. Then read the exam task in exercise 2 and the model answer below. Complete the table using the information in the model answer.

My town is very historic and we get a lot of visitors. There are several things I would improve to attract even more tourists. Here are three of the most important.

First of all, I would improve the parking. In my opinion, this is the most important thing because the town is always full of cars. If there was a car park on the edge of town, tourists could leave their cars there and get a bus into the centre. It would be easier for them and they could enjoy less crowded streets.

Secondly, I would cut the entrance price to museums and art galleries. The tickets can be very expensive, especially for families. If prices were cheaper, more tourists would visit these attractions.

Finally, I would arrange some interesting things for children to do in the park. If there were more activities for children, more families would come to the town.

To conclude, I would improve parking, reduce prices and provide things for children to do. All these things would attract more tourists to our town.

Preparation

1 Read the task and the letter. What is the writerâ€™s main reason for complaining? Choose a, b or c.

Your local council has decided to stop a free bike hire scheme in your town centre. Write a letter of complaint about this decision.

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the decision to stop the free bike hire scheme in our town. This scheme has been very popular, especially among young people, and I cannot understand why the council wants to stop it.

I object to the decision mainly because the bike hire scheme encourages people to cycle1â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ going by car or bus.2â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ cycling is good for the environment and good for peopleâ€™s health, we want as many people as possible to do it.

I understand that here have been some problems with vandalism. However, I do not think a small number of vandals should be able to change the councilâ€™s policy. Surely it is possible to install security cameras,3â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦â€¦ the bikes are not damaged so often.

In conclusion, I believe the bike hire scheme benefits the environment and the residents, and should continue.

Your faithfully,

Penny Wentworth

Writing Strategy

Make sure you use a variety of different structures in your writing. You can form complex sentences by joining two clauses together with a conjunction (although, because, if, or,etc.). Use different conjunctions depending on the meaning of the clauses they introduce.

Strategy

When writing an article that gives opinions about an issue, it is a good idea to give some examples to illustrate your point(s).

1. Read the Strategy. Underline the phrases used to introduce examples in the sentences below.

3  Children need to learn about important environmental problems like global warming and climate change when they are at primary school.

4  We can do lots of things to help prevent burglaries, such as putting in alarms and locking all our windows.
